Bail Bond Information for Haines County

After booking into Haines County jail, a judge typically sets bail at arraignment (often within 24–72 hours). Families often work with a licensed bail bondsman. A common commercial bond fee is about 10% of the bail amount (non-refundable). Example: $10,000 bail → roughly $1,000 premium, subject to local rules.

If the person cannot afford bail, they may request a reduction hearing or public defender.

For hearing schedules, contact the Haines County court.

Visitation Rules at Haines County Jail

Policies vary. Before visiting Haines Borough Police Department Temporary Holding Facility, confirm:

  • Dress code: Facilities restrict clothing that resembles uniforms
  • Video visits: Many jails offer remote options — ask when you call
  • Children: Minors usually need an accompanying adult

What to Expect After Arrest in Haines County

Typical steps after arrest in Haines County:

  1. Booking — fingerprints, photo, property inventory
  2. Medical screening — before general population housing
  3. Classification — housing based on charges and history
  4. Arraignment — first court appearance; bail often set here
  5. Transfer — serious cases may move to a state facility

Frequently Asked Questions — Haines County Inmate Lookup

How do I find out if someone is in Haines County jail?

There is no verified public online roster URL on file for Haines County. Call the Haines Borough Police Department at (907) 766-2121 or use the Alaska Department of Corrections site for state custody. We do not treat web search results as official jail records.

How long does booking take in Haines County?

Booking often takes 2–8 hours depending on volume. Weekends and holidays can delay when a name appears in any published system.

Can I visit an inmate at Haines County jail?

Usually yes if the facility allows visits and the person is eligible. The main facility is located at 211 Haines Hwy, Haines, AK 99827. Contact Haines Borough Police Department Temporary Holding Facility for hours, ID rules, and dress code. Video visitation may be available.

What if the person is not in the county jail system?

They may be in state custody — check the Alaska DOC. For federal charges use the BOP inmate locator.

How do I send money to an inmate in Haines County?

Most facilities use a commissary vendor (for example JPay, Securus, or Access Corrections). Confirm the vendor and limits with Haines Borough Police Department Temporary Holding Facility before sending funds.
